Recent work supports diagnosing negative quality beyond random-negative margins. A [2024 comparative study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) found aggregate metrics conceal head/mid/tail disparities and sampling-dependent popularity bias. [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) identifies premature hard-negative training and fixed hardest-item selection as failure modes; proposes uniform warm-up followed by global candidate recall and curriculum difficulty. These findings support testing gradual, mixed negative sampling within one NextItNet model; they do not establish that semantically similar unobserved products are genuine negatives.

The [TREC 2025 product-recommendation annotation framework](https://huggingface.co/datasets/trec-product-search/product-recommendation-2025/discussions/1/files) distinguishes functional substitutes from compatible substitutes, and complementary products with known versus unknown compatibility. An actionable diagnostic proposal: construct auditable contrast sets from existing titles/descriptions using lexical overlap and explicit attributes—specific matches versus broad topical matches, near-duplicates, substitutes, and possible complements. Record supporting text spans; mark missing specifications and immediate purchase intent unknown. Measure paired score margins, ranking reversals, and evidence coverage separately from benchmark HR@10. Treat duplicate/redundancy and compatibility flags as semantic proxies, not observed dissatisfaction: repeat purchases may be intentional, and textual similarity does not establish practical fit. Keep actual feedback findings separate from proxy-generated hypotheses; absent feedback, report no feedback-derived conclusions.
